title: Robot loop basics
concept: A robot senses, estimates, decides, acts, then measures the result.
lab: Run the simulator for one minute and write what each dashboard metric means.
proof: Add one screenshot or one paragraph explaining the robot loop.

title: Coordinate frames
concept: Robot position is easier to reason about when x, y, and heading are explicit.
lab: Change the starting pose and predict which direction the robot will move first.
proof: Record the starting pose and whether your prediction was right.

title: PID tuning
concept: Proportional gain can reduce error quickly, but too much can cause oscillation.
lab: Try low, medium, and high P gains. Compare overshoot and settling behavior.
proof: Write the best gain values you found and why.

title: Noisy sensors
lab: Increase range noise and explain how it changes confidence.
proof: Save a note comparing low-noise and high-noise runs.

title: Waypoint planning
concept: A planner breaks a goal into smaller reachable targets.
lab: Add or move a waypoint in code and observe how the controller reacts.
proof: Document the waypoint list and the final path shape.

title: Robot state logs
concept: Logs turn vague robot behavior into evidence.
lab: Use the simulator metrics to explain one failure or inefficiency.
proof: Write one bug-style note with expected behavior, actual behavior, and a guess.

title: ROS2 mental model
concept: ROS2 systems are often organized as nodes that publish and subscribe to topics.
lab: Map simulator pieces to possible nodes: controller, sensor, planner, dashboard.
proof: Create a small node-topic-message table in the daily log.

title: Testing robot math
concept: Pure math helpers are easier to test than UI behavior.
lab: Read `src/robotics.test.ts` and add one new edge-case test.
proof: Commit the test and note what bug it would catch.

title: Obstacle thinking
concept: Robots must handle the world they did not ask for.
lab: Add a new obstacle and describe how the current robot fails around it.

title: Internship story
concept: A strong portfolio connects code choices to robotics outcomes.
lab: Write a README paragraph beginning with: I built this to learn...
proof: Update the README with one measurable result.
